metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: Specify a partition scheme that guarantees each slice stays below the ceiling regardless of issue distribution (e.g. adaptively subdivide any slice that itself hits the ceiling), rather than a fixed status/date/key-range cut that a single dense slice can still overflow.
evidence: fetch_paging.py:145 — `if accumulated + len(page) >= _ACLI_CEILING:` fires per single ACLI query (per slice), so any one slice exceeding the ceiling re-raises
The active query alone is already ~1,050→1,200 (fetcher.py:51-52); a status-based partition offers no guarantee any single status stays bounded as REB grows
Plan states the goal 'no single ACLI call approaches the ceiling' but names only fixed partitions that do not adaptively bound slice size
findings.finding: The three named partition strategies (slice by status / updated-date window / key range) are not intrinsically bounded below the ceiling: a single dense status or date window can itself exceed 1,200 and re-raise SilentTruncationError(reason='ceiling'), so the fix would still couple capacity to distribution rather than fully decoupling it from project size.
findings.location: Section 'Why raising the constant is the WRONG fix' — 'slice by status, by updated-date window, or by key range, and union the results'
scenarios: One workflow status (e.g. a large 'In Progress' backlog) grows past 1,200 → ceiling re-raises even after partitioning
A busy update-day makes one date window exceed the ceiling
findings.suggested_fix: Prefer an adaptive/recursive partition: fetch a slice, and if it approaches the ceiling, subdivide that slice further (e.g. bisect the date/key range) and recurse. This makes bounded-slice-size a guarantee rather than an assumption about distribution.

findings.checklist_item: Add an acceptance criterion (and test) proving the union of partition slices is complete and non-overlapping under concurrent mutation — e.g. use a mutation-stable partition key or a coverage-completeness assertion — not just per-slice anti-truncation checks.
evidence: The AC covers cursor-stall/offset-stall/short-page 'at the seam' but not whether the union of slices is COMPLETE and NON-OVERLAPPING under concurrent mutation
fetcher.py:97 jql_done_recent uses `ORDER BY updated DESC` — the fetch is already sensitive to `updated` changing mid-scan; a date-window partition inherits this hazard
Absence: plan does not state how boundary-straddling / mutated-mid-scan issues are prevented from falling between slices
findings.finding: The plan does not address partition COVERAGE/GAP correctness across slices: with slice boundaries on a mutable field (updated-date window, statusCategory, or key range under concurrent activity), an issue mutated between slice fetches can fall into a coverage gap (never fetched by any slice) or straddle two slices, producing a silent partial the guard cannot detect.
findings.location: Section 'Why raising the constant is the WRONG fix' + AC line on anti-truncation seam guarantees
scenarios: An issue's `updated` timestamp changes between fetching window A and window B such that it is in neither snapshot → invisible to the pass, a candidate for the deletion/absence path
A status transition between the statusCategory!=Done slice and Done slice re-runs (already partially mitigated by the atomic per-project merge, but a within-active sub-partition reintroduces it)
findings.suggested_fix: Partition on an immutable/monotone key (e.g. issue key/id range) rather than a mutable field like `updated` or status, or snapshot a fixed boundary set first, so no issue can migrate between slices mid-scan; assert union coverage against total count.

findings.checklist_item: Name the concrete ACLI/REST capability used to MEASURE each query's true matched count on a surface that truncates at the ceiling (e.g. a verified --count/approximate-count flag, the REST search `total`, or a documented method of narrowing the JQL below the ceiling and summing slices), and confirm it exists against ACLI --help/Jira docs before relying on AC-1.
evidence: Plan AC: 'The current matched-issue count for each reconciler query is MEASURED and recorded ... alongside the 2026-05-26 baseline, establishing growth vs. query-widening as cause.'
adapters/jira/acli.py:434 docstring: 'ACLI Go has no offset flag, so --paginate fetches all results in one call.'

adapters/jira/acli.py:445-481: search_issues issues `jira workitem search --jql <jql> --paginate --json`, parses a bare list (:466-467), caches all, and returns a client-side slice — no count/total from the real path.
The ceiling (JRACLOUD-94632) truncates the same --paginate fetch, so a naive row-count of an over-ceiling query is itself truncated — the measurement and the failure share one mechanism.
Evidence class: Partially-verified — the integration exists and is in use, but the specific count-measurement surface the AC depends on is unconfirmed against ACLI --help/docs.
findings.finding: AC-1 asserts measuring 'the current matched-issue count for each reconciler query' but does not name a capability that returns a TRUE count on a surface that silently truncates. The real ACLI search_issues runs `jira workitem search --jql --paginate --json` (one call, no offset flag, returns a bare list), and that single --paginate call is exactly what JRACLOUD-94632 truncates at 1200 — so for any query above the ceiling, counting returned rows cannot yield the true matched count, which is the number the growth-vs-widening decision turns on.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — AC-1 ('current matched-issue count for each reconciler query is MEASURED'); Confirm-before-fixing section
scenarios: An engineer runs the reconciler queries to record counts, sees exactly 1200 (or the truncated slice length), and cannot distinguish 'grew to 1300' from 'grew to 3000' — mis-reads growth-vs-widening and picks the wrong partition granularity.
The active query already matches >1200; the recorded 'count' silently equals the ceiling and the baseline comparison is meaningless.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the measurement method explicitly: either (a) use the REST search endpoint's `total` field (verify it is exposed and not itself capped), or (b) partition each query into sub-ceiling JQL slices first and sum the per-slice counts — which also doubles as the partition-design probe. Record which was used and mark the evidence class Verified once confirmed against --help/docs.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the expected slice count / per-run ACLI call budget for the chosen partition and confirm it stays within the vendor rate limit on the hourly schedule.
evidence: 'slice by status, by updated-date window, or by key range, and union the results'
hourly schedule against a vendor-limited ACLI (JRACLOUD-94632)
absence: no per-run API-call budget or slice-count bound stated
findings.finding: The partition strategy multiplies the number of ACLI calls per reconcile run (union of slices = N calls instead of paged single query), but the plan states no bound on slice count or per-run call budget against the vendor rate limit.
findings.location: 'Why raising the constant is the WRONG fix' — partition-the-query direction
scenarios: A key-range or date-window partition producing dozens of slices multiplies ACLI calls each hour, risking a new rate-limit / latency failure mode
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note bounding slices (e.g. status-based partition yields a small fixed number of queries) and an AC that the partitioned run's total ACLI call count stays under the rate limit.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record the chosen partition axis and its rationale (including how the union preserves anti-truncation guarantees) in a module comment/ADR alongside the fix.
evidence: absence: no AC requiring documentation of the partition-strategy choice
the existing constant carried its own history comment (:19-24), setting a precedent for recording rationale in-code
findings.finding: The chosen partition scheme (status / date-window / key-range) is a novel architectural decision affecting fetch semantics, but the plan does not require capturing the decision in an ADR / design doc / module comment.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria + 'Why raising the constant is the WRONG fix'
scenarios: A future maintainer hitting a third growth event needs to know why this partition axis was chosen and how the seam preserves guarantees

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify that the live-run AC is proven together with the synthetic larger-than-ceiling capacity test, so a green run cannot be attributed to a shrunken/narrowed working set instead of the fix.
evidence: The capacity AC uses a synthetic larger-than-ceiling working set (a test), while the live-run AC does not pin the live matched count
competing-cause note: 'If the query widened, narrowing it may be the correct and much smaller fix' — narrowing could green the live run without partitioning
findings.finding: The 'rebar bridge run completes without SilentTruncationError(reason=ceiling)' criterion could pass merely because the working set shrank or the query was narrowed, without the size-independence fix actually being present — it does not assert the live matched count still exceeds the old ceiling at verification time.
findings.location: AC: 'rebar bridge run completes against the live REB project without raising SilentTruncationError(reason="ceiling")'
scenarios: If cause turns out to be query-widening and it is narrowed, the live-run AC greens without the size-independence fix, yet other ACs still demand partitioning — the live run alone does not prove capacity decoupling
findings.suggested_fix: Note explicitly that the size-independence criterion is proven by the synthetic-larger-than-ceiling test, and the live run is a regression check, not the proof of decoupling.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that the partitioned union yields an EXACTLY-complete, de-duplicated snapshot across slice boundaries — a test with issues placed on/adjacent to slice seams (date-window edge, key-range edge) asserting the union set equals the full expected set with no dropped or duplicated issues.
evidence: AC: 'a test that drives the fetch path with a working set materially LARGER than the ceiling and asserts a complete, non-truncated snapshot' — 'complete' is asserted but boundary completeness/dedup across slices is not called out
Plan: 'slice by status, by updated-date window, or by key range, and union the results' — union of overlapping/adjacent slices can drop or duplicate issues at boundaries
The seam ACs test that guards still raise, not that the union yields exactly the expected issue set
findings.finding: The partition-and-union fix introduces slice-boundary correctness risk (an issue could be missed if it falls between two date-window/key-range slices, or double-counted if slices overlap), but no acceptance criterion asserts the unioned snapshot is COMPLETE and DEDUPLICATED across seams. The seam ACs cover the anti-truncation guards raising, and one AC asserts 'non-truncated' for an oversized set, but none proves union correctness (no dropped/duplicated issues at the seam).
findings.location: Acceptance criteria (the larger-than-ceiling test AC and the seam-guard AC)
scenarios: An issue updated exactly at a date-window boundary is fetched by neither slice and silently vanishes from the snapshot — the exact silent-partial class the guard exists to prevent, but now reintroduced at the union layer
Overlapping key-range slices double-count an issue, corrupting the reconcile pass
findings.suggested_fix: Add: 'A test places issues exactly on and adjacent to each partition boundary (date-window edge, key-range/status seam) and asserts the unioned snapshot equals the complete expected issue set with no omissions or duplicates.'
